title: Logical interface
description: What every target of one document shares: the signals the specification names, the rules that turn a signal into what the document reads, and the outputs as the document produces them. A binding is split into this and a target profile (`sce_targets.split`), and a target builds from the two. Nothing in it is a platform's: no address, no record field, no counter protocol, and no number for a symbol. A closed set crosses by name, so a signal lists its symbols and an output lists the document's own values; a number for a symbol is a platform's code and lives in the platform's interface model.

document.description: Path to the SCXML this interface is for, relative to the interface file.

producedValue.description: A value the document produces for an output: the name of one of its own enumeration's variants, or a literal of a text, number or truth-value output (which may be the empty text). It is the document's own, never a platform's number for a symbol.

signal.description: An input from the surroundings, by the name the specification uses: a closed set of symbols, or a number, a text or a truth value.

values.description: The symbols, and nothing the platform numbers them by.

statechartInput.description: A signal that changes to `becomes` sends `event`.

statechartCarriedInput.description: A signal whose value the machine is told: `event` is sent with the signal's value as the data field `carries`, whenever the signal changes (and, with `becomes`, only when it changes to that symbol).

transformInput.description: What the document reads from a signal: a comparison of its symbol, or the signal itself handed over as the document's type. A signal that is not reporting reads as `when_absent`, and without one the round cannot be computed. A closed set is handed to a document input of an enumeration type, by name; it is never handed as a number.

logicalInput.description: A state the specification names and a platform encodes however it does (the target profile's `protocols`); here it is a plain true or false.

event.description: A statechart is told the state as the data of this event, sent whenever the state changes.

statechartOutput.description: The last send to `sent.processor` in a round names the value; else `when_nothing_sent`; else the output is not written that round.

attributes.description: Constants the specification states for the output, by a logical name.

transformOutput.description: What the document computes: one of `values` (a closed set, by the document's own names), the value as it is (`passthrough`), or a value the document keeps to itself (`internal`).

holds_last.description: A value the document produces outside `values` is no announcement: the output keeps the last value it announced, and before there is one it has none.
